anderson.q: Non-lifting cylinder. The pressure coefficient on the surface at θ = 90° is:
anderson.detail: On the surface V_θ = −2V∞ sin θ so V²/V∞² = 4 sin²θ; at 90° this is 4 and C_p = 1 − 4 = −3.

anderson.q: Non-lifting flow round a cylinder: if V∞ doubles the shape of the streamlines:
opts: changes only far from the body
anderson.explain: V_r and V_θ are both proportional to V∞ so the velocity direction at every point is unchanged.

anderson.q: Flow round a cylinder with fixed circulation Γ: if V∞ doubles the shape of the streamlines:
anderson.explain: V_θ has an extra term Γ/(2πr) that does not scale with V∞.

anderson.q: Spinning cylinder, V∞ = 30 m/s, ρ = 1.23 kg/m³, lift 6 N/m. The circulation is:
25 ft of 2 in diameter struts at 120 mi/h sea level (ρ = 0.002377 slug/ft³) with C_D = 1 on the frontal area. The strut drag is:
anderson.explain: D = q S C_D with S = length × diameter.
anderson.detail: q = 36.81 lb/ft²; S = 25 × (2/12) = 4.167 ft²; D = 153.4 lb (Solution Manual 153 lb).

anderson.q: Flow round a cylinder, ψ₁ = 0 on the surface, ψ₂ through (1.2R, π/2), streamlines equally spaced upstream. The streamline ψ₃ passes over the top at r/R equal to:
anderson.explain: ψ₃ = 2ψ₂ and ψ(r) = V R (r/R − R/r) at θ = 90°.

anderson.q: A cylinder in a sea-level wind tunnel; compressibility starts to matter when the local velocity exceeds 250 mi/h. The corresponding free-stream velocity (V_max = 2V∞) is:
anderson.detail: V∞ = 250 mi/h / 2 = 125 mi/h = 55.88 m/s. The local Mach number is then 0.33.
